title: Not All Unlabeled Data Are Equal: Unlabeled Data Selection for Semi-Supervised QSAR Modeling with Large Chemical Repositories
abstract: arXiv:2610.22025v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is particularly attractive in domains where labels are expensive to obtain, while unlabeled examples are readily available. Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship (QSAR) modeling, which predicts molecular biological activity from chemical structure, is one such domain. Obtaining activity measurements requires costly wet-lab experiments, resulting in small labeled datasets, while chemical repositories such as ChEMBL contain millions of unlabeled molecules. Despite this apparent suitability, the potential of large chemical databases to improve QSAR models via SSL remains largely unexplored. Furthermore, it is unclear how unlabeled data should be selected in realistic SSL settings with genuine unlabeled data. translated_abstract: 半监督学习（SSL）在标签获取成本高昂而无标签样本容易获得的领域中尤其具有吸引力。定量构效关系（QSAR）建模——即根据化学结构预测分子生物活性——正是这样一个领域。获取活性测量数据需要昂贵的湿实验室实验，导致标注数据集规模较小，而ChEMBL等化学数据库中却包含数百万个无标签分子。尽管表面上二者高度契合，但大型化学数据库通过SSL改进QSAR模型的潜力在很大程度上仍未被探索。此外，在包含真实无标签数据的现实SSL设置中，应如何选择无标签数据也尚不清楚。我们使用从ChEMBL提取的10个QSAR数据集以及超过40万个无标签分子的数据池，对无标签数据选择进行了系统性研究。为此，我们评估了三种已有的
tldr: 该论文首次在真实半监督学习场景下，利用ChEMBL的10个QSAR数据集和40余万无标签分子池，系统研究了如何从大型化学数据库中选择无标签数据以改进QSAR模型，揭示了并非所有无标签数据都同等有价值。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first systematic study of unlabeled data selection from large chemical repositories (over 400,000 molecules) for semi-supervised QSAR modeling across 10 ChEMBL datasets, demonstrating that not all unlabeled data are equally valuable.
